issues.description: Constructor mismatch: the class de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest.PersonResource has a constructor whose parameter type differs between artifacts. The template (and the problem description's architecture) expects a constructor accepting a PersonService for dependency injection (public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). The solution repository's PersonResource constructor instead declares a String parameter (public PersonResource(String personService) { this.personService = personService; }), which does not match the field type PersonService and will cause a compilation error and confuse students about correct controller wiring.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution repository, change the PersonResource constructor signature to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This restores correct dependency injection and matches the template/problem design.

issues.description: Constructor parameter type for PersonResource is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and template expect a PersonService dependency to be injected into PersonResource (constructor parameter type: PersonService). In the solution repository PersonResource declares the constructor parameter as a String (public PersonResource(String personService)) while the field is typed as PersonService (private final PersonService personService). This mismatch (PersonService vs String) prevents a clear mapping from the described Application layer dependency (PersonService) to the REST resource, would cause a compile-time type error in the solution, and confuses students about how dependency injection supplies the PersonService.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution repository, change the PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field, e.g.: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This restores consistent types and the intended dependency injection behavior.
